# September 4, 2026

## Summary {.unnumbered}

**The 8/27 K_init sweep's log-likelihood and BIC were in-sample, not cross-validated.** An advisor
asked directly whether they were, and the honest answer at the time was "not sure, probably" — they
were not. A genuine held-out survival log-likelihood and a bi-cross-validated genomics log-likelihood
now exist alongside the existing in-sample criteria, reported separately since they answer different
questions. See (§2).

**Building the held-out survival log-likelihood surfaced a real, pre-existing orientation bug** in
`fit_cox_on_yf()`'s post-loop sign-correction, independent of anything else in this session's work. It
does not affect any previously-reported external C-index or K_eff number, but it did affect the
in-sample BIC/log-likelihood values reported on 8/27. Fixed at the two places it mattered
(`compute_bic.R`, `compute_cv_loglik.R`); the shared fitting function is left unchanged and the issue
documented at the source. See (§2).

**Six criteria now disagree on K_init, and the disagreement is itself informative, not a problem to
resolve.** ELBO and in-sample BIC prefer K_init=3; held-out survival log-likelihood drifts toward
larger K; bi-CV genomics log-likelihood favors K≈4; external C-index plateaus from K_init=7. External
C-index is the only one of the five testing generalization to genuinely independent cohorts, and is
the right one to lead with. See (§2).

**The K_init=11/13 external-C dip is real and not a multistart artifact.** A stated, falsifiable
prediction that 15-restart best-ELBO multistart would remove the dip was WRONG — the SVD init already
has the best ELBO of all 15 restarts at every K tested. Why these two specific K values land on a
worse solution remains open. See (§2.3).

**Cohort membership now reaches the survival coefficients, not just the genomics reconstruction.** A
new `beta_cohort_id` argument lets each latent factor carry a different survival coefficient per
cohort, distinct from the existing `cohort_id` (genomics offsets) and `strata_id` (baseline hazard)
extensions — all three are now inventoried and composable. See (§3).

this chapter rather than documentation:

## §2 — What the log-likelihood and BIC actually were, and a cross-validated replacement

```{r setup}
library(knitr); library(dplyr)
BM <- "../../../results/benchmark_sim/outputs"
rd <- function(p) if (file.exists(p)) read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL

ksweep <- rd(file.path(BM, "k_init_sweep", "k_init_sweep_results.csv"))
dip    <- rd(file.path(BM, "k_init_sweep", "k_init_multistart_dip_results.csv"))
cbc    <- rd(file.path(BM, "cohort_beta_comparison", "cohort_beta_comparison_results.csv"))
```

### §2.1 — What was actually computed on 8/27

The 8/27 figure's log-likelihood and BIC (`code/compute_bic.R`'s `compute_joint_ll_bic()`) are
**in-sample**: the model is fit on all 273 training patients, then scored on those same 273 patients.
Three limitations of this specific BIC, verified directly in `compute_bic.R`'s roxygen and repeated
here because they explain why it and a genuine held-out check can disagree:

- The Cox term is a *partial* likelihood with the baseline hazard profiled out. Its effective sample
  size is the event count (139 in this training set), not the 273 patients `log(n)` charges it
  against.
- `df = K_init·(n+p+1)` is charged by the CAVI starting K, not by ARD's K_eff — deliberate (K_eff is a
  post-hoc classification of the same fit, not a smaller model), but it means BIC's complexity penalty
  does not track what ARD actually keeps.
- `log(n)·df` applies a single, `n`-scaled penalty against a genomics reconstruction term whose
  effective sample size is `n·p` (≈563,000 entries), not `n`.

No "cross-validated BIC" was built. BIC's `log(n)` penalty and cross-validation both correct for
in-sample optimism, under different asymptotic justifications (BIC vs. AIC) — combining them
double-corrects the same thing. The right comparison is: keep the in-sample BIC with the caveats
above, and report a genuinely held-out criterion alongside it.

### §2.2 — A held-out survival log-likelihood, and a bi-cross-validated genomics log-likelihood

New `code/compute_cv_loglik.R`, two criteria, reported separately and never combined into one number:

- **`cv_survival_loglik()`**: stratified 5-fold CV, fit on 4/5 of the training patients, scored on the
  held-out 1/5 via `eta_new = (Y_test·F)·beta` — the exact YFB prediction formula, so no train/test
  mismatch. Each fold's orientation is fixed from **training** concordance only, never from the
  held-out fold's own outcomes (that would leak).
- **`bicv_genomics_loglik()`**: bi-cross-validation (Owen & Perry 2009), holding out row AND column
  blocks jointly. Ordinary row-wise held-out genomics scoring is not well-defined here — projecting a
  held-out patient's loadings from that same patient's own expression and then scoring against it
  reuses the data being scored, so the apparent fit improves in K regardless of real structure. There
  is also no missing-data (NA/mask) machinery anywhere in the CAVI loop, so Wold-style single-cell
  masking was not an option.

**Building the held-out survival log-likelihood found a real bug, independent of this new code.**
Orienting each CV fold required replicating `fit_cox_on_yf()`'s own post-loop sign-correction rule.
Doing so exposed that the rule checks `concordance(Surv(time,status) ~ eta)` without `reverse = TRUE`
— per `survival::concordance()`'s own documentation, its formula method assumes a larger predictor
means a *longer* survival by default, the opposite of a Cox risk score. Verified empirically: a fit
with true training concordance of 0.90+ read as "already fine, don't flip" under the existing check,
because the check itself has the direction backwards.

This does not affect any previously-reported external C-index (`oriented_cindex()`'s `max(c, 1-c)` is
invariant to exactly this sign ambiguity) or K_eff (`classify_factors()`'s `abs(EBeta)` threshold, also
sign-invariant), so the K_init=7 recommendation — which rests on external C-index — is unaffected. It
does affect Cox partial log-likelihood, which is not sign-invariant, so the 8/27 BIC/log-likelihood
values were computed on a systematically mis-oriented survival term. The shared fitting function
(`fit_cox_on_yf.R`) is left unchanged — fixing it would flip `EBeta`'s sign for every existing fit, and
every currently-reported result that depends on that sign already uses a convention that does not need
the check to be correct. `compute_bic.R` and `compute_cv_loglik.R` instead re-derive the correct
orientation themselves; the issue is documented prominently at the source.

### §2.3 — Six criteria, six different questions

```{r ksweep-fig, fig.cap="K_init consensus sweep, six panels. ELBO and in-sample BIC (top left, top middle) score training-data fit dominated by the genomics term (n·p ≈ 563,000 numbers vs. 139 events); held-out survival log-likelihood (bottom left) and bi-cross-validated genomics log-likelihood (bottom middle) are new this session; external C-index (bottom right) is the only criterion testing generalization to genuinely independent cohorts."}
knitr::include_graphics("../figs/2026-09-04_k_init_sweep_6panel.png")
```

Reading each panel as what it actually measures, not as a single number to argmax:

- **ELBO / in-sample BIC** score training-data fit combined across genomics reconstruction and
  survival into one number, and the genomics term is roughly 1,400x larger by raw entry count. They
  are really answering "does this factor reduce genomics reconstruction error enough to justify its
  complexity cost," almost regardless of what it does for survival — which is exactly why K_init=3
  (`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) ksweep$K_eff_total[ksweep$K_init==3] else 3` kept factors, no ARD pruning
  headroom at all) looks best to them even though its external C-index
  (`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", ksweep$mean_external_c[ksweep$K_init==3]) else "0.594"`)
  sits near the K_init=2 floor.
- **Held-out survival log-likelihood** measures only survival generalization, on the *same* training
  cohort (one 5-fold split, not repeated across seeds). It drifts upward with K
  (`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", min(ksweep$cv_survival_logPL_per_event, na.rm=TRUE)) else "-3.24"`
  at the low end to
  `r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", max(ksweep$cv_survival_logPL_per_event, na.rm=TRUE)) else "-3.16"`
  at the high end, per event) — a real signal, but a noisy single-split one, best read as "more
  factors don't obviously hurt held-out survival fit here" rather than a precise argmax at K=19.
- **Bi-CV genomics log-likelihood** measures only genomics generalization, and says something
  different: past K≈4, additional factors mostly capture structure that does not hold up under
  held-out gene×patient blocks — a caveat purely about the genomics side, unrelated to survival.
- **External C-index** is the only criterion testing generalization to genuinely independent cohorts
  (different institutions, platforms, years) — the actual deployment question, and the right one to
  lead with. It plateaus from K_init=7
  (`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", ksweep$mean_external_c[ksweep$K_init==7]) else "0.627"`)
  through K_init=20, with a nominal peak at K_init=12
  (`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", ksweep$mean_external_c[ksweep$K_init==12]) else "0.630"`,
  a +0.003 difference from K_init=7 — not a meaningfully different result). K_init=7 is the smallest
  K_init on that plateau, which is the parsimony argument, not a claim that ELBO/BIC concur.

The disagreement is not a discrepancy to resolve. Each criterion is answering a genuinely different
question — training fit dominated by genomics, held-out survival fit on the training cohort, held-out
genomics fit on the training cohort, and generalization to new cohorts entirely — and trusting the one
closest to the actual deployment question (external C-index) over the others is the correct read, not
an arbitrary choice among five noisy estimates of the same thing.

### §2.4 — The K_init=11/13 dip does not survive multistart

The sweep above shows external C-index dropping sharply at K_init=11
(`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", ksweep$mean_external_c[ksweep$K_init==11]) else "0.599"`)
and K_init=13
(`r if (!is.null(ksweep)) sprintf("%.3f", ksweep$mean_external_c[ksweep$K_init==13]) else "0.539"`),
against an otherwise flat K_init=7..20 plateau, coinciding with the two worst ELBOs in the sweep and
with `K_survival_active` jumping from 2 to 3. Before running anything, this was stated as a falsifiable
prediction: if the dip is a single-init CAVI local-optimum artifact — the documented failure mode
elsewhere in this project, for K=5/6 (2026-08-19) and K=2/4 (2026-07-13) — a 15-restart best-ELBO
multistart search should find a better solution at K_init=11/13 that lands back on the plateau.

```{r dip-table}
if (!is.null(dip)) {
  kable(dip[, c("K", "best_idx", "n_init", "best_elbo_full", "K_survival_active", "mean_external_c")],
        col.names = c("K_init", "Best restart", "n restarts", "Best ELBO", "K survival-active", "Mean external C"),
        digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 4))
} else {
  cat("(k_init_multistart_dip_results.csv not found)")
}
```

**The prediction is wrong.** At every K_init in {10,...,15}, restart 1 (the SVD init) already has the
best ELBO of all 15 restarts — every random restart collapses to essentially zero active factors, so
best-of-multistart reproduces the single-init sweep exactly, dip included. The K_init=11/13 dip is a
real, reproducible property of the SVD-initialized fit at those two specific K values, not a fixable
initialization artifact. Why K_init=11 and K_init=13 specifically converge to a 3-survival-active-factor
solution with much worse external validity, while no other K_init in the 7-20 range does, is left open
(`ROADMAP.md`); deflation-init or warm-starting from the converged K_init=7 solution are the natural
next things to try, not attempted here.

## §3 — Cohort membership in the survival term

Three cohort-aware model components now exist and are independent, composable, and separately
maintained:

| Component | Added | What it does | Effect on beta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cohort_id` | 2026-05-22 | Fixed indicator columns appended to L/F, absorbing per-gene platform offsets in genomics reconstruction | `beta_cohort = 0` by construction — never reaches survival |
| `strata_id` | 2026-07-15 | Stratified Cox partial likelihood — cohort-specific baseline hazard | Beta stays shared across strata |
| `beta_cohort_id` | 2026-09-04 | Cohort-specific survival coefficients beta_k^(c) | The only one where beta itself varies by cohort |

$$
\eta_i = \sum_k (YF)_{ik} \cdot \beta_k^{c(i)}
$$

- $\eta_i$: the Cox linear predictor for patient $i$
- $(YF)_{ik}$: the observed projection score of patient $i$ onto factor $k$
- $\beta_k^{c(i)}$: the survival coefficient for factor $k$ under patient $i$'s cohort $c(i)$

The $C$ cohort coefficients per factor are partially pooled through one shared EBNM prior (one
vectorized `ebnm()` call per factor across cohorts, not $C$ independent calls) — the "consensus
factors are more reproducible" idea, made operational rather than assumed.

`cohort_id` was last benchmarked 2026-05-22 at K=20 under an older preprocessing pipeline, where it
lost for YFB (mean external C 0.544 → 0.539) — never under the current recommended config until now.
The table below re-benchmarks it there directly, alongside the new `beta_cohort_id` extension, all
three combined, and the two-step EBMF→Cox baseline — sanity-gated first against
`desurv_comparison_results.csv` (D4: 0.6267, K_eff=2 — matched exactly).

```{r cohort-beta-table}
if (!is.null(cbc)) {
  kable(cbc[, c("arm", "K", "K_survival_active", "K_eff_total", "mean_external_c")],
        col.names = c("Arm", "K", "K survival-active", "K_eff total", "Mean external C"),
        digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 4))
} else {
  cat("(cohort_beta_comparison_results.csv not found)")
}
```

**This is a clean null result for every cohort-aware extension tested here, under the current
recommended config.** None beats the plain joint model (0.6267):

- **`cohort_id` alone is the worst arm** (0.5431), even worse than the two-step baseline (0.6008), and
  `K_survival_active` drops from 2 to 1 — the genomics-offset columns compete with, rather than
  coexist alongside, the biological factors that carry real survival signal. This extends the
  2026-05-22 finding (cohort_id lost for YFB under older preprocessing) to the current D4/K_init=7
  config directly, closing that open question.
- **`beta_cohort_id` alone is the best of the three cohort-aware arms** and clears the two-step
  baseline (0.6132 vs. 0.6008), but still trails the plain joint model by −0.0135. Cohort-specific
  survival coefficients are not actively harmful the way `cohort_id` is, but they do not currently add
  value over a single shared coefficient — on this training set (n=273, 139 events, C=2 cohorts), there
  is not enough per-cohort signal for the partial-pooling structure to earn back the extra model
  complexity.
- **Combining all three extensions (0.6060) does not recover the gap** either — it sits between
  `beta_cohort_id` alone and the two-step baseline.

Reported as a finding, not smoothed over: the cohort-aware extensions built to date do not improve
external validity for this dataset's size and cohort structure (two training cohorts). Whether a
larger or more heterogeneous training set (more than two cohorts, larger per-cohort n) would change
this is an open question, not addressed here — the full Stage 3 analysis (bootstrap CIs on the
pairwise differences, leave-one-study-out, and the separate supervised-vs-unsupervised factor
comparison) is still pending and would sharpen whether −0.0135 is distinguishable from noise.

## §4 — Where the value-add goes next

Multi-modality extension (methylation, matched multi-view data) is out of scope here: no such data
exists under `PDAC_DATA_ROOT` (all 7 datasets are gene-level expression/protein), and
`preprocess_merged_cohorts()` row-binds patients into one n×p matrix, so same-patient feature blocks
from different modalities are structurally unrepresentable in the current pipeline. This is a
prerequisite for that direction, not a decision against it.
